t.6.9.1: Then Nikumbha, Rabhasa, the mighty Sūryaśatru, Suptaghna, Yajñakopa, Mahāpārśva and Mahodara…
t.6.9.2: And the unassailable Agniketu, and the rākṣasa Raśmiketu, and Indrajit, the mighty son of Rāvaṇa, possessed of great splendour.
t.6.9.3: Then Prahasta, Virūpākṣa, the mighty Vajradaṃṣṭra, Dhūmrākṣa and Atikāya, and the rākṣasa Durmukha as well…
t.6.9.4: Iron clubs, sharp-edged spears and darts, javelins, pikes and battle-axes, bows together with arrows, and large, sharpened swords.
t.6.9.5: Seizing their weapons and springing up, all the rākṣasas, exceedingly enraged and blazing as it were with fiery energy, spoke to Rāvaṇa.
t.6.9.6: Today we shall slay Rāma, and Sugrīva together with Lakṣmaṇa, and the wretched Hanumān, by whom Laṅkā was assailed.
t.6.9.7: Having restrained all of them as they took up their weapons, and having made them sit down again, Vibhīṣaṇa, with joined palms, spoke these words.
t.6.9.10: But how do you wish to assail him, who is ever vigilant, eager for victory, firmly established in his strength, master of his anger and hard to overcome?
t.6.9.9: Bold exploits, my dear, succeed against those who are heedless, those already beset by foes, and those struck down by fate, when they are undertaken with due method after careful examination.
t.6.9.11: Having leapt across the terrible ocean, lord of rivers great and small, Hanumān has accomplished a deed most difficult. Who could even conceive of it?
t.6.9.12: O night-rangers, the strength and valour of others are beyond measure; contempt for one's foes should never, in any way, be shown rashly.
t.6.9.13: And what wrong had Rāma done to the king of the rākṣasas before, that he carried off from Janasthāna the wife of that illustrious one?
t.6.9.15: Vaidehī is the cause of this, and a very great danger may arise for us. She who was carried off must be given up; since it was done only for the sake of a quarrel, why should she not be?
t.6.9.16: It is not fitting for us to make a pointless enmity with that valiant one who follows dharma; let Maithilī be given back to him.
t.6.9.8: My dear, the wise declare that an aim which cannot be attained even by the three means calls for those occasions of valor as fitting.
t.6.9.17: Before he tears apart with his arrows this city, with its elephants and horses and teeming with many jewels, let Maithilī be given back to him.
t.6.9.18: Before that most terrible, vast and invincible army of monkeys assails our Laṅkā, let Sītā be given back.
t.6.9.19: For the city of Laṅkā would perish, and all the heroic rākṣasas too, if Rāma's beloved wife is not given back of our own accord.
t.6.9.20: Because of our kinship I entreat you; do as I say. I speak what is beneficial and wholesome: let Maithilī be given back to him.
t.6.9.14: If Khara, who had overstepped all bounds, was slain by Rāma in battle, it is because living beings must of necessity protect their lives as far as their strength allows.
t.6.9.21: Before the king's son looses for your destruction his unfailing arrows, very firm, with fresh tips and feathered shafts, gleaming like the rays of the autumn sun, let Maithilī be handed over to Dāśaratha.
t.6.9.22: Abandon your anger, which destroys happiness and righteousness, and embrace dharma, which increases joy and fame. Be gracious, so that we may live on together with our sons and kinsmen; let Maithilī be given back to Dāśarathi.
